notifications.title: CLEAVE v3.3.2.0 is available
notifications.message: Config Helper — a new button on each Reconcile unit that sets up the whole configuration by clicking through your own files. Choose a file and click its header row, click the first and last column of the compare range on two sheets that are lined up and scroll together, build the key with a live preview, then check the pairing against real rows before you run. Apply hands it to the Reconcile form as a normal configuration. Settings also loses its developer section. Includes everything from 3.3.1.1.

notifications.title: What's new in CLEAVE v3.3.2.0
notifications.message: Configuring a reconcile no longer starts with an empty form. The Config Helper asks for one thing at a time against the real sheet: click the row that holds your column names, click the first and last column of the range — with both sheets lined up pair above pair, scrolling together, and skipped columns cut out of the layout — then click the columns that make the key and watch it assemble, padded zeros highlighted inside the key itself. Before you run, the Match Tolerance step reads real rows through the engine's own comparison and shows them side by side: three key tallies you can open and list, the four granular match options as switches that re-read the sample, jump-to-next-difference, and click a pair to ignore it. The last step picks the destination and the sheets. Everything it produces is an ordinary configuration on the Reconcile form, so the readiness rail, the key preview and Simulate still apply.
